Emmanuel Mignot, MD, PhD, Receives the Lasker Award for Discovering the Cause of Narcolepsy  

Through genetic and immunological studies, the Stanford Medicine sleep researcher found that narcolepsy stems from a deficiency of orexin in the brain, opening the door to new sleep therapies. 

Read about Mignot 

 

Study Ties Estrogen-Based Menopausal Hormone Therapy to Lower Alzheimer’s Risk 

Some studies have reported that menopausal hormone therapy raises dementia risk. A new study that analyzed Alzheimer’s-disease hallmarks in autopsied brains indicates the opposite.

Health Insurance Plans: Frequently Asked Questions About Insurance

  • About
  • About

Find answers to common questions about health insurance. If you have additional questions, please contact your insurance provider directly.

I want to receive my care at Stanford Health Care. Will my insurance plan cover me?

Before you receive care at Stanford Health Care, we strongly recommend contacting your insurance company directly. You will likely need to provide them with our NPI and tax ID numbers to verify their participation as in-network providers for your specific insurance plan. If they’re out-of-network, be sure to find what you may need to spend out of your own pocket for care you know you’ll need now and would like to have in case your health needs change. 

Our physicians and hospital each have a NPI and tax ID number:

  • Stanford Health Care Physicians Group NPI: 1437292927
  • Stanford Health Care Physicians Tax ID: 77-0465765
  • Stanford Health Care Hospital NPI: 1871543215
  • Stanford Health Care Hospital Tax ID: 77-0465765

TIP: Whenever you speak with health plan representatives, it is beneficial to write down the name and reference number of your conversation for future reference.

What are important questions I should ask my insurance company about my coverage?

When it comes to health insurance coverage, it’s essential to know what is most important to you, such as:

  • Cost: Will you be paying a monthly premium or pay at point-of-service?  Will you need to pay out-of-pocket before your plan begins covering your services?  

  • Access: Do you have a particular doctor(s) you want to see for primary care and/or specialty care? Do you prefer receiving your care at a specific medical facility (hospital, urgent care, clinic)? What network does my plan utilize?

  • Medications: Will your plan cover any medications you’re taking now?

  • Health services: Do you need a plan that covers acupuncture, physical therapy or other services? Find out how many times you can use these services per year.  
How can your Patient Financial Clearance team help me?

Our Patient Financial Clearance team is available to answer your questions related to insurance coverage, including any out-of-pocket costs and pre-authorization before your appointment or procedure. 

To best prepare for your call, be sure to have:

  • Your current health insurance card
  • Our NPI and Tax ID 
  • Information related to your upcoming visit or procedure
  • Your list of questions
  • Your preferred means for taking notes

Please contact us with your questions. We’re glad to help. 

Patient Financial Clearance
Phone: 650-724-4445
Toll Free: 1-877-291-7335
Mon – Friday, 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.

Whom do I contact if I do not have insurance?

Stanford Healthcare offers several programs for patients who are underinsured or who do not have insurance coverage. 

We have financial counselors who can assist you by assessing your liability, connecting you with available funding sources such as Medi-Cal and Medicare, or determine if you’re eligible for charity care or financial hardship treatment. 

To learn more, visit Financial Counseling. 

Why didn’t my insurance pay for my medical services?

You should receive an explanation of benefits (EOB) from your insurance company explaining how your claim was processed and/or paid. It will indicate the amount billed, paid, denied, discounted, not covered, and the amount owed by the patient.

If you have any questions about your EOB, be sure to contact your insurance provider.    

What if I can’t afford to pay my insurance bill?

If you are unable to pay your bill, Stanford Healthcare offers several programs for patients who are underinsured or who do not have insurance coverage.  Learn more about our financial assistance and financial counseling services.

Our physicians and hospital each have a NPI and tax ID number: Stanford Health Care Physicians Group NPI: 1437292927 Stanford Health Care Physicians Tax ID: 77-0465765 Stanford Health Care Hospital NPI: 1871543215 Stanford Health Care Hospital Tax ID: 77-0465765 TIP: Whenever you speak with health plan representatives, it is beneficial to write down the name and reference number of your conversation for future reference.

mainEntity.name: What if I can’t afford to pay my insurance bill?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are unable to pay your bill, Stanford Healthcare offers several programs for patients who are underinsured or who do not have insurance coverage. Learn more about our financial assistance and financial counseling services.

mainEntity.name: How can your Patient Financial Clearance team help me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our Patient Financial Clearance team is available to answer your questions related to insurance coverage, including any out-of-pocket costs and pre-authorization before your appointment or procedure. To best prepare for your call, be sure to have: Your current health insurance card Our NPI and Tax ID Information related to your upcoming visit or procedure Your list of questions Your preferred means for taking notes Please contact us with your questions. We’re glad to help. Patient Financial Clearance Phone: 650-724-4445 Toll Free: 1-877-291-7335 Mon – Friday, 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.

MyHealth - Access Your Health Information

Get Connected to Your Health & Care Team

With MyHealth, managing your care has never been easier for both your regular checkups and hospital stay. Make appointments and message your doctors. View test results, pay medical bills, renew prescriptions, and more.

Have a question? Visit our MyHealth FAQ to get answers fast.

Create New Account

   

MyHealth for Outpatient Care

MyHealth for Outpatient CareBusy lives need a healthy dose of convenience. MyHealth lets you request appointments, message your doctors – even trend your general health.

MyHealth for Inpatient Care

Stay informed with care updates and information during your hospital stay. Share this information with close family through the MyHealth app.

What MyHealth Offers

Stay Connected to Your Health Information

  • View your test results
  • Review after visit summaries and doctor notes
  • Keep track of your biometrics
  • Access information regarding your health

Communicate with Your Care Team

  • Send and receive secure messages
  • Receive reminders about your care
  • Request prescription refills

Manage Your Care on Your Time

  • Schedule appointments
  • Conduct video visits
  • View and pay medical bills

SIGN IN

Forgot Username? Forgot Password? Contact the MyHealth Help Desk

   

MyHealth Tips

Get the MyHealth app on your Android phone or iPhone

Managing care from your phone is quick and easy with MyHealth. Download for iOS or Android today.

Get care conveniently with video visits

Video visits are a great way to see your doctors without traveling to a clinic. Talk to your clinic to learn more.

Skip the line at your next visit with eCheck-in

Manage co-pay in advance, notify the care team when you arrive, and more (at select clinics). Take a look

   

Share Access for Caregivers

Share Access allows family members or caregivers to see other adults’ medical information and help manage their care. It’s the best way to let patients share information with caregivers as needed, while maintaining their rights to privacy.

Individuals with Share Access can:

  • View portions of the patient's health record
  • View test results for the patient
  • Request appointments for the patient
  • Send message to care team on patient’s behalf

   

Be Informed and Gain Insights During Your Hospital Stay

MyHealth now offers Hospital View, which is activated if you are admitted to Stanford Hospital. MyHealth will help guide you through your hospital stay by providing you with features that will keep you informed about your care.

  • Learn more about your medications
  • Get prompt test results
  • Track progress toward discharge
  • Meet mobility and pain goals
  • Request services like massage, art therapy, or music therapy
  • Learn more about members of your care team

Stanford Health Care MyHealth App

Download the MyHealth app and manage your care from your iPhone or Android phone.

Important Information About COVID-19 Testing & Billing

During the coronavirus pandemic, Stanford Health Care remains your partner in health.

If you need help paying your medical bill, we're here for you. Payment plans and financial assistance are available for people who can't pay their balance in full.

Federal, state, and local regulations may dictate that patients are not liable for the cost of COVID-19 testing. If a patient's insurance is out-of-network with Stanford Health Care, the following cash price would be payable in accordance with Stanford Health Care's self-pay discount policy:

  • COVID-19 Antibody (IGG or IGM); (CPT 86769): $84
  • COVID-19 Probe Detection by DNA or RNA; (CPT 87635): $156
  • COVID-19 Specimen Collection (Swab); (HCPCS C9803): $15.60

Financial Counseling

Financial Counseling is available to help you navigate the financial component of getting care at Stanford Health Care. As part of the Patient Access Services team, financial counselors are dedicated to serving as a resource to you and your family by:

  • Explaining your insurance coverage and benefits
  • Estimating your financial responsibility for services not covered by insurance
  • Identifying possible ways for you to pay for your care if you do not have adequate funds or health insurance
  • Helping you identify and obtain coverage for government programs, where available
  • Addressing questions or concerns regarding your insurance coverage and financial assistance

Reach a financial counselor at 844-498-2900 from Monday – Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Financial counselors strive to make the financial concerns surrounding your care as stress free as possible, so you can focus on what is most important—your health.

Learn more

New Patient Refunds Process

We are excited to inform you that we will be using a new payment platform, Recipient Select, to allow you to choose your preferred method for receiving your patient refund via a secure web portal. Payments made by credit card will be refunded to the original form of payment. If the payment was made in a different form or the card is no longer available, refunds will be issued through a secure Bank of America web portal called Recipient Select. 

Patients can choose the preferred method for receiving the refund. When applicable, the patient will receive an e-mail from Stanford Health Care with a link to the portal and instructions to create a profile and select the preferred payment method. 

Patients will have 5 days from the date of the e-mail to complete the selection.  If not completed within 5 days, a check will be mailed to the patient.

As part of the Patient Access Services team, financial counselors are dedicated to serving as a resource to you and your family by: Explaining your insurance coverage and benefits Estimating your financial responsibility for services not covered by insurance Identifying possible ways for you to pay for your care if you do not have adequate funds or health insurance Helping you identify and obtain coverage for government programs, where available Addressing questions or concerns regarding your insurance coverage and financial assistance Reach a financial counselor at 844-498-2900 from Monday – Friday, 9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m. Financial counselors strive to make the financial concerns surrounding your care as stress free as possible, so you can focus on what is most important—your health. Learn more New Patient Refunds Process We are excited to inform you that we will be using a new payment platform, Recipient Select, to allow you to choose your preferred method for receiving your patient refund via a secure web portal. Payments made by credit card will be refunded to the original form of payment. If the payment was made in a different form or the card is no longer available, refunds will be issued through a secure Bank of America web portal called Recipient Select. Patients can choose the preferred method for receiving the refund. When applicable, the patient will receive an e-mail from Stanford Health Care with a link to the portal and instructions to create a profile and select the preferred payment method. Patients will have 5 days from the date of the e-mail to complete the selection. If not completed within 5 days, a check will be mailed to the patient.
